title: How should planning results become a reviewable decision?
problem: Current output exposes tasks and waves but does not give the reviewer enough context to compare directions or understand why one should be approved.

stance.reason: The user supplied the desired outcome while the implementation space benefits from independent alternatives and evidence-led synthesis.

decision.question: Which review format should become the portable default?
decision.outcome: A reviewer can choose a direction quickly without losing evidence, nuance, or implementation consequences.
nonGoals: Implement the selected direction during brainstorming
Preserve every conversational turn in the final artifact
constraints: Works offline as a local file
Uses the same artifact across AI hosts
Remains readable on mobile and desktop

evidence.claim: Generic key/value cards make recommendations, evidence, and metadata look equally important.
evidence.implication: The review needs an explicit visual hierarchy tied to decision semantics.

evidence.claim: The minimal quick fixture contains no alternatives or risks, so its HTML cannot demonstrate a deep planning experience.
evidence.implication: Use a separate representative artifact for human-facing examples.

evidence.claim: A comparison table is effective for repeated attributes, but not for explaining complete option narratives.
evidence.implication: Pair a scan-friendly matrix with detailed approach dossiers.

evidence.claim: A deterministic static document will be sufficient for the first review workflow.
Reviewers will prefer every execution task expanded by default.
evidence.implication: Keep task disclosure reversible and validate the default with real usage.

openQuestions.question: Should deep-plan execution details open by default?
When should annotations justify an interactive runtime?

ideas.title: Executive decision dossier
ideas.summary: Lead with recommendation, evidence, tradeoffs, and the approval question.
assumptions: Reviewers need a fast decision spine before implementation details.

ideas.title: Exploration workbench
ideas.summary: Expose how raw ideas became clusters, candidates, and a recommendation.
evidence: A final option list hides idea provenance and discarded connections.
assumptions: Visible convergence increases trust without requiring the full chat transcript.

ideas.title: Interactive review application
ideas.summary: Add annotations, filters, and persisted reviewer state.
evidence: Large plans can benefit from navigation and collaboration.
assumptions: The value of interaction would outweigh portability costs.

ideas.title: Structured Markdown record
ideas.summary: Prioritize diffability and host-native preview over controlled presentation.
evidence: Markdown is broadly readable across AI hosts.

ideas.title: Decision JSON with specialized projections
ideas.summary: Keep one canonical artifact and render different human views without duplicating truth.
evidence: The portable state layer already persists arbitrary JSON evidence.
assumptions: A deterministic renderer can preserve semantic fidelity.

ideas.title: No generated HTML
ideas.summary: Return the decision only in conversation and avoid renderer maintenance.
assumptions: Conversation history remains durable and reviewable.

clusters.name: Durable decision truth
clusters.insight: The durable artifact should be machine-readable while its review projection is optimized for the human decision.

clusters.name: Visible reasoning
clusters.insight: Planning needs traceability while brainstorming needs provenance and an explicit convergence path.

clusters.name: Capability boundary
clusters.insight: Interactive review is valuable only after static review proves insufficient; chat alone is not a durable review surface.

approaches.name: Semantic decision dossier
approaches.thesis: Give each decision concept a purposeful visual treatment while keeping the artifact deterministic and static.
approaches.description: Lead with the recommendation and approval gate, then compose evidence, architecture, options, risks, validation, and execution from specialized server-side rendering functions.
approaches.whyLens: Optimize for informed human approval without sacrificing portability.
benefits: No external runtime or asset dependency
Semantic markup can be tested directly
tradeoffs: New fields need an intentional presentation
whatBreaks: Unknown fields fall back to a less polished generic appendix
Large artifacts still require editorial discipline
approaches.whenToPick: Pick when the primary job is reviewing and approving a generated engineering decision.
approaches.failureMode: The renderer grows into a collection of ornamental cards without preserving a clear decision narrative.

approaches.name: Interactive review application
approaches.thesis: Turn every plan into a filterable, annotatable client-side application.
approaches.description: Bundle a component runtime that supports collapsed sections, reviewer annotations, filtering, and persisted decisions.
approaches.whyLens: Optimize for collaborative review and future workflow automation.
benefits: Powerful navigation for very large artifacts
Natural path to annotations and approval state
approaches.whenToPick: Pick when annotation, collaboration, and persisted interaction are validated requirements.
approaches.failureMode: The review tool becomes a product of its own before the underlying decision contract is mature.

approaches.name: Structured Markdown record
approaches.thesis: Prioritize diffability and host-native rendering over a controlled visual review experience.
approaches.description: Generate a rigorous Markdown decision record with tables and headings, then delegate presentation to the active AI host or repository viewer.
approaches.whyLens: Optimize for the smallest durable artifact and easiest source review.
tradeoffs: Complex comparisons become harder to scan
approaches.whenToPick: Pick as the universal fallback when a host cannot open local HTML.
approaches.failureMode: The output regresses into a long wall of prose that hides the decision spine.

recommendedDefault.reason: It delivers the requested richer review experience while preserving the portable, zero-dependency contract.
recommendedDefault.acceptedTradeoff: We accept more presentation code now and defer interactive annotations until they are proven necessary.
recommendedDefault.nextAction: Validate the dossier with rich fixtures at mobile and desktop widths.

shortlist.reservation: Requires more intentional renderer code and schema discipline.
Adds a runtime and product surface before interaction is validated.
Cannot guarantee a consistent, enriched review hierarchy.

dissent.case: Markdown is simpler to diff, audit, and open in every host, and it avoids maintaining presentation code.
dissent.trigger: Choose it as the primary path if local HTML opening proves unreliable across supported hosts.

cheapestExperiment.question: Can a reviewer identify the recommendation, its strongest evidence, and the rejected alternatives within two minutes?
cheapestExperiment.method: Render one representative deep plan and brainstorm, then inspect them at 320, 768, 1440, and 1920 pixels.
cheapestExperiment.successSignal: The reviewer can answer the decision question without opening the execution appendix and no viewport has body overflow.
cheapestExperiment.cost: Two deterministic fixtures, semantic assertions, and one browser inspection pass.

directionGate.question: Approve the semantic decision dossier as the default and keep Markdown as fallback?
